sections.title: The letter Ö
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (Ö) /øː/. Its main sound is a vowel, which means open air with no touch. You hear it in (Öl) /ʔøːl/, which means oil. This letter has two sounds.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, push your tongue forward and make your lips into a tight circle. Voice is on, so your throat shakes. For the second sound, lower your jaw slightly and keep your tongue forward. Put a finger before your lips to feel them push forward firmly.

sections.title: Reading the spellings
paragraphs: In long or stressed open syllables, you say the sound in (schön) /ʃøːn/. In short closed syllables, you say the sound in (öffnen) /ˈʔœfnən/. A syllable is one beat of a word. When two consonants follow, the sound is usually short as in (Köpfe) /ˈkœpfə/.

sections.title: Avoiding common pitfalls
paragraphs: Do not replace this letter with the vowel sound in bird. Do not glide two sounds together like the vowel in boat. Keep your tongue forward and keep your lips in a steady circle. Hold the shape still until you finish speaking.
